title: Measured comparison with 2024-2026 template-matching, pose and few-shot counting methods
question: Where does this project's NCC matcher (stable core and research pipeline) beat or lose to PoseMatch-TDCM, GeCo2 and an OpenCV matchTemplate baseline on the same inputs, scored by one independent scorer, with accuracy, time and memory kept apart?

Per case the median over blocks.

measurement.memory: peak RSS per process; ours named Metal allocations; MPS driver allocation; CUDA max allocated/reserved; never added
measurement.host: timed phases hold timing-lock-round50-<phase>.txt in the shared notes folder for their whole duration, wait while another session's lock exists, record load and >=50% CPU processes per worker (recorded, not gated)

hypotheses.H1: Group A positives: (a) ours_fullgpu_k3 strict recall >= TDCM-adapted (primary pipeline, CPU) strict recall on every case, and >= OpenCV's on every case OpenCV completed; (b) on pooled A positives the median position and angle errors of ours_fullgpu_k3's association pairs are below TDCM-adapted's; (c) pooled box recall at IoU >= 0.5 of ours_fullgpu_k3 >= GeCo2's. H1 passes when (a), (b) and (c) pass.
hypotheses.H2: B2: GeCo2 AP50 > ours_fullgpu_k3 AP50 on the FSCD-147 test boxes (falls back to count MAE against FSC points if the mirror is not used).
hypotheses.H3: C tiny templates under the official 36x36 weights (rewritten per the user; the paper's 12x12 result is cited, not reproduced): TDCM-adapted pooled strict recall on the tiny-template positives >= ours_fullgpu_k3's.
hypotheses.H4: On >= 4096x4096 multi-object scenes (many128_pose, many512_pose, many8k_512), same M4 Pro: ours_fullgpu_k3 per-image call time < TDCM-adapted CPU per-image call time on each scene.
hypotheses.H5: A negatives (empty_scene, constant_source, 7 wrong-template scenes): every ours arm reports 0 false positives; competitors' false positives reported, GeCo2 N/A.

decision: Measurement and comparison round: no default, GUI or CURRENT_BEST recommendation changes. The report states each hypothesis and lists where each method wins by group; failures, N/A cells and every failed worker stay in the tables.
exploratory_disclosure: Phase 1 ran every method on two smoke pairs (tdcm_demo, many128); those outputs shaped the adapters (TDCM size range and single target, GeCo2 CPU fix, scipy) and are not phase-2 data.

While the tools were written (before this draft), TDCM-adapted ran once on many128 with a 0.5 peak threshold (4 targets, CPU and MPS identical); that is why the threshold is now chosen on development scenes. many128 is a scored A case. The refactored TDCM and GeCo2 workers were regression-checked on tdcm_demo and many128 (outputs identical to phase 1).
Phase 1 runner smoke overlapped round 49's dev_calibrate lock at 09:50:07Z (<1 s), disclosed in both rounds.
The S2 list regenerated by the published rule has 9 more rows than the published file; the published file is used.
